regeln: Within each spoken phase use multiple distinct relevant shots, roughly 3-5 seconds each for Shorts; long videos can allow purposeful longer demonstrations. Preserve continuous narration and accurate subtitle timing.
A zoom, crop, subtitle change or decorative background does not count as a new motif. Never fill missing images with candles, unrelated stock or background-only frames.
Show the main image prominently; avoid tiny repeated photos in a mostly empty vertical frame. Preserve genuine evidence and important image details.
For AI Tools Explained identify the exact tool briefly, then show genuine interface views and different source-supported examples. Never present stock or an illustration as a real tool result.
Use original urban painted open-world-game poster styling for fictional scenes and presenters; no copied game characters. Match narrated action and era.

Clear speech and readable captions alone do not make a professional video. Inspect useful motif changes and narration-image alignment over the entire video. Missing main imagery is a substantial defect.
Include mandatory spoken like, share and save calls at the correct format-specific positions. Do not replace this requirement with a different CTA.

AI Tools Explained is for viewers with a practical task. Do not read parameter counts, architecture names, pipeline tags, context lengths or benchmark claims as a substitute for useful explanation. Explain the human task, the source-supported action and a concrete limit. A generic trending-tools question failed story review twice; prefer a specific visual workflow.

The user confirmed original presenter references on 2026-10-05: Business Origin Stories uses the blue-eyed man with a fedora, grey suit, dark tie and gold pocket watch; AI Tools Explained uses the black-haired man with black leather jacket and glowing cyan glasses. Preserve identity and typical clothing, vary action and setting.

Introduce the correct presenter at the opening and bring that same presenter back during the video in useful actions. Do not confine the figure to the ending. Do not replace original channel figures with different fictional people; anonymous period workers remain clearly illustrative supporting people, never a real-founder likeness.

Prefer vivid original painted open-world-game scenes to long holds on lifeless documentary photos. Preserve factual accuracy and show authentic tool examples briefly as evidence. Camera moves alone are not new motifs or full character animation.

The user confirmed on 2026-10-05 that both new delivered videos are much better than before. Preserve the original painted world, recurring channel identity, matching main imagery, music and useful scene changes. The long-term quality target remains 10/10; the user did not give these videos a numeric score. Do not replace their actual AI scores or the existing 7/10 delivery threshold with the aspirational target.

From 2026-10-11 both channels require at least 18 genuinely distinct relevant motifs in every new 35-45-second Short. Show different subjects, actions, useful details or genuine source-backed tool examples that match the spoken words. Repeated offices or presenter poses, zooms, crops and changed labels do not count as new motifs. This is now a production requirement, replacing earlier planning targets for 82-90-second pilots. Preserve the original recurring presenter and painted-world style.

Show genuine tool demonstrations—real interface screens or README media—whenever the tool is mentioned; never use symbolic icons or illustrations as a substitute for real results.
Structure videos around a specific human-task problem and a tangible, surprising result; replace dry technical documentation or academic phrasing with the direct benefit the AI achieves for the user.
Include at least 18 distinct, relevant motifs in every 35–45-second Short, counting only unique subjects or actions rather than zooms, crops, or label changes.
Start with a high-impact hook in the first three seconds that promises a clear, task-based benefit and avoids generic introductory statements.

Maintain the original painted open-world-game aesthetic for all fictional scenes, ensuring characters, settings, and actions are original and consistent rather than using stock clips or lifeless photos.

Ensure the tool’s logo and name visually dominate thumbnails and hero shots; the channel presenter (black-haired, leather jacket, cyan glasses) must remain secondary to the branding to ensure immediate utility recognition.
Scale pacing appropriately: use rapid motif changes for Shorts and deliberate, longer demonstrations for long-form content, ensuring narration remains aligned with the visual pace.
Focus scripts strictly on user workflows and practical tasks; omit technical jargon, pipeline tags, or parameter counts unless they are essential to a practical step.
Include mandatory spoken 'like, share, save' CTAs at the correct, format-specific positions without substitution.
Integrate the presenter consistently throughout the video in useful actions rather than confining them to the opening or closing.
Verify all scripts against primary tool documentation and treat viewer feedback as data for identifying pacing or narrative weaknesses without overgeneralizing single defects.
Ensure the presenter's appearance remains consistent with the established identity (black-haired man, leather jacket, cyan glasses) while varying their specific actions and the setting.

## What is Docling ?

Docling simplifies document processing by parsing diverse formats — including advanced PDF understanding — and providing seamless integrations with the generative AI ecosystem.

## Features

- 🗂️ Parsing of [multiple document formats][supported_formats] including PDF, DOCX, PPTX, XLSX, HTML, EPUB, Apple Pages, Numbers & Keynote, WAV, MP3, WebVTT, Box Notes, email formats (EML, MSG), images (PNG, TIFF, JPEG, ...), LaTeX, DocLang, plain text, and more
- 📑 Advanced PDF understanding incl. page layout, reading order, table structure, code, formulas, image classification, and more
- 🧬 A unified, expressive [DoclingDocument][docling_document] representation format
- ↪️ Various [export formats][supported_formats] and options, including Markdown, HTML, WebVTT, DocLang, [DocTags](https://arxiv.org/abs/2503.11576) and lossless JSON
- 📜 Support for several application-specific XML schemas including [DocLang](https://doclang.ai), [USPTO](https://www.uspto.gov/patents) patents, [JATS](https://jats.nlm.nih.gov/) articles, and [XBRL](https://www.xbrl.org/) financial reports.
- 🔒 Local execution capabilities for sensitive data and air-gapped environments
- 🤖 Plug-and-play [integrations][integrations] incl. LangChain, LlamaIndex, Crew AI & Haystack for agentic AI
- 🔍 Extensive OCR support for scanned PDFs and images
- 👓 Support for several Visual Language Models, such as ([GraniteDocling](https://huggingface.co/ibm-granite/granite-docling-258M))
- 🎙️ Audio support with Automatic Speech Recognition (ASR) models
- 🔌 Connect to any agent using the [MCP server](https://docling-project.github.io/docling/usage/mcp/)
- 🌐 Run Docling as a service with the [API server](https://docling-project.github.io/docling/usage/api_server/) (docling-serve)
- 💻 Simple and convenient CLI

### What's new

- 🎬 Parsing of video files (MP4, AVI, MOV, MKV, and WebM) with an ASR transcript and representative keyframes
- 📄 Parsing of ODF (OpenDocument Format) files for text documents (`.odt`), spreadsheets (`.ods`), and presentations (`.odp`)
- 💼 Parsing of XBRL (eXtensible Business Reporting Language) documents for financial reports
- 📧 Parsing of email files (`.eml`, `.msg`)
- 📚 Parsing of EPUB (Electronic Publication) files for e-books
- 🍎 Parsing of Apple Pages (`.pages`) documents, Numbers (`.numbers`) spreadsheets and Keynote (`.key`) presentations
- 📝 Parsing of plain-text files (`.txt`, `.text`) and Markdown supersets (`.qmd`, `.Rmd`)
- 📊 Chart understanding (Barchart, Piechart, LinePlot): convert them into tables or code and add detailed descriptions

### Coming soon

- 📝 Metadata extraction, including title, authors, references & language
- 📝 Complex chemistry understanding (Molecular structures)

## Quickstart

### 1. Install

> **Note:** Python 3.9 support was dropped in docling version 2.70.0. Please use Python 3.10 or higher.

Works on macOS, Linux and Windows environments for both x86_64 and arm64 architectures.

More [detailed installation instructions](https://docling-project.github.io/docling/getting_started/installation/) are available in the docs.

## 2. Convert a document (CLI)

This generates a .md file in the current directory containing structured document content.

You can also use 🥚[GraniteDocling](https://huggingface.co/ibm-granite/granite-docling-258M) and other VLMs via Docling CLI:

## 3. Python usage (recommended)

More advanced [usage](https://docling-project.github.io/docling/usage/) and [configuration](https://docling-project.github.io/docling/getting_started/installation/) options.

## Documentation

Check out Docling's [documentation](https://docling-project.github.io/docling/) for details on
installation, usage, concepts, recipes, extensions, and more.

## Examples

Go hands-on with our [examples](https://docling-project.github.io/docling/examples/),
demonstrating how to address different application use cases with Docling.

## Integrations

To further accelerate your AI application development, check out Docling's native
[integrations](https://docling-project.github.io/docling/integrations/) with popular frameworks
and tools.

## Get help and support

Please feel free to connect with us using the [discussion section](https://github.com/docling-project/docling/discussions).

## Technical report

For more details on Docling's inner workings, check out the [Docling Technical Report](https://arxiv.org/abs/2408.09869).
